Order rows by sort-tile-recursive packing

Source: R/extendr-wrappers.R
ga_str_order.Rd

Returns the row order that sort-tile-recursive (STR) packing gives the bounding box centres of geometry. Pass it to [ to sort an array or a data frame so that nearby rows sit together.

Usage

ga_str_order(geometry, node_size = 16)

Arguments

geometry

a GeoArrow geometry array

node_size

how many rows share a leaf

Value

an integer array of 1 based row numbers, the same length as geometry

Details

ga_str_order() sorts the rows by the x of their centres, cuts them into vertical slices of node_size times the square root of the number of leaves, and sorts each slice by y. That is the leaf order an STR packed R-tree with node_size entries per node uses, the same packing RTree$new(sort = "str") builds.

ga_str_order() breaks ties by the original row order, and puts rows with a null or empty geometry last, in their original order.

See also

Other index: KDTree, RTree, ga_envelope(), ga_hilbert_order(), ga_knn_join(), ga_set_thread_pool(), ga_sparse_dwithin(), ga_sparse_knn()

Examples

nc <- as.data.frame(read_shapefile(
  system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf")
))
ord <- as.vector(ga_str_order(nc$geometry, node_size = 4))

# the first slice runs south to north along the west of the state
head(nc[ord, "NAME"])
#> [1] "Clay"         "Cherokee"     "Macon"        "Transylvania" "Jackson"     
#> [6] "Polk"
